### nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d {#sec-example-laminar-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d}

This example case is based on the forced Poiseuille flow case of [[`laminar/poiseuille3d`](/examples/laminar/poiseuille3d/poiseuille3d.qmd)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}[`laminar/poiseuille3d` (@sec-example-laminar-poiseuille3d)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}, where several non-Newtonian viscosity models, such as Power-Law, Casson, and Carreau--Yasuda, can be applied.
The identical pressure drop is applied for all models where the other model parameters are converted accordingly for easy comparison of the viscosity model impact.
Note that the Carreau--Yasuda model is not in a validated state yet.

#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I$, the inside of a pipe of diameter $D$ times $\R_{\geq 0}$, is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^3$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a generalized Newtonian fluid with constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$, driven by the constant pressure gradient $G = -\partial_x p$ as a body force,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= \frac{1}{\rho} \nabla \cdot \left( 2 \mu(\dot\gamma) \mathbf{S} \right) + \frac{G}{\rho} \mathbf{e}_x \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I,
\end{align}
with the strain rate tensor $\mathbf{S} = \tfrac{1}{2} (\nabla \vel + \nabla \vel^\top)$ and the shear rate $\dot\gamma = \sqrt{2 \mathbf{S} : \mathbf{S}}$.
`VISCOSITY_MODEL` selects the dynamic viscosity $\mu(\dot\gamma)$:

- `NEWTONIAN`: $\mu = \mu_0$,
- `POWER_LAW`: $\mu = K \dot\gamma^{\,n - 1}$ with the power-law index $n$ and the consistency index $K$,
- `CASSON`: $\sqrt{\tau} = k_0 + k_1 \sqrt{\dot\gamma}$ for the shear stress $\tau = \mu \dot\gamma$, where $k_0^2$ is the yield stress and $k_1^2$ the Casson viscosity,
- `CARREAU_YASUDA`: $\mu = \mu_\infty + (\mu_\text{zero} - \mu_\infty) \left( 1 + (\lambda \dot\gamma)^a \right)^{(n - 1)/a}$.

For the Newtonian, power-law and Casson models, the steady solution in the pipe is known analytically and is used to measure the error. For the Carreau–Yasuda model, the example compares with the power-law profile with the index $0.708$.

#### Boundary conditions

The pipe is periodic in $x$, and the pipe wall $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ (MN 2) is a no-slip wall,
$$
    \vel = \mathbf{0} \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}} \times \I.
$$
The body force $G / \rho$ drives the flow instead of an inlet and an outlet.
The simulation starts from the analytical velocity profile of the selected model.

#### Domain

The pipe has the diameter $D = 1\,\mathrm{mm}$ and the length $L = 3\,\mathrm{mm}$, and its axis runs along $x$ through $y = z = D/2$.
The fluid properties are those of blood: the density $\rho = 1060\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ and, for the Newtonian model, the dynamic viscosity $\mu_0 = 4.0755 \cdot 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}$.
The pressure gradient
$$
    G = \frac{16 \mu_0^2 Re}{\rho D^3}
$$
gives the Newtonian fluid the maximum velocity $u_\text{max} = Re\, \mu_0 / (\rho D) = 0.38\,\mathrm{m/s}$ for $Re = 100$.
The same $G$ drives all models. The consistency index $K$ of the power law and the constant $k_1$ of the Casson model are derived from $\mu_0$ and $G$, so that the models are comparable.

`prepareGeometry()` marks the cells inside a cylinder slightly longer than the pipe as fluid (MN 1) and the cells around it as wall (MN 2).

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid with the lattice spacing $\Delta x = D / N$, where $N = 31$ cells resolve the diameter of the pipe.

The LBM collision operator is a BGK operator with a body force ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), together with the D3Q19 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)): `ForcedBGKdynamics` for the Newtonian model, and `PowerLawForcedBGKdynamics`, `CassonForcedBGKdynamics` and `CarreauYasudaForcedBGKdynamics`, whose relaxation time follows the local shear rate, for the others.
The descriptor stores the force and the local relaxation frequency in every cell.
The pipe wall (MN 2) is treated with the Bouzidi boundary, `setBouzidiBoundary()`, which takes the exact position of the curved wall between the lattice nodes into account ([Define Boundary Method](/content/06_initial_boundary.qmd#sec-defineBoundaryMethod)).

The corresponding lattice is defined inside the case definition in `case.h` as in @lst-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-case.

::: {#lst-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<
  NavierStokes, Lattice<double, descriptors::D3Q19<descriptors::FORCE,descriptors::OMEGA>>
>;
```
Case definition for the `nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d` example.
:::

The unit converter `UnitConverterFromResolutionAndRelaxationTime` derives the time step size from the resolution, the lattice relaxation time and the characteristic velocity of the selected model, the maximum of its analytical profile.
The parameters are given in @tbl-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-params.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EOC` | | `false` | not used by the simulation itself; the convergence study is a program of its own, see below |
| `VISCOSITY_MODEL` | | `NEWTONIAN` | viscosity model: `NEWTONIAN` (0), `POWER_LAW` (1), `CASSON` (2), `CARREAU_YASUDA` (3) |
| `RESOLUTION` | $N$ | $31$ | cells per pipe diameter $D$ |
| `EOC_RESOLUTIONS` | | $41, 61, 81, 101$ | resolutions of the convergence study |
| `DOMAIN_EXTENT` | $L \times D \times D$ | $3 \times 1 \times 1\,\mathrm{mm}$ | size of the pipe |
| `LATTICE_RELAXATION_TIME` | $\tau$ | $0.64265$ | lattice relaxation time |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DENSITY` | $\rho$ | $1060\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ | density |
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | $T$ | $0.3\,\mathrm{s}$ | simulated time |
| `REYNOLDS` | $Re$ | $100$ | Reynolds number of the Newtonian flow, which sets $G$ |
| `DYNAMIC_VISCOSITY` | $\mu_0$ | $4.0755 \cdot 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ | viscosity of the Newtonian model |
| `PRESSURE_DROP` | $G$ | $16 \mu_0^2 Re / (\rho D^3)$ | pressure gradient |
| `POWER_LAW_EXPONENT` | $n$ | $0.65$ | power-law index |
| `CONSISTENCY_INDEX` | $K$ | derived from $\mu_0$ and $G$ | consistency index of the power law |
| `K0` | $k_0$ | $0.07\,\mathrm{Pa^{1/2}}$ | Casson constant, $k_0^2$ is the yield stress |
| `K1` | $k_1$ | $\sqrt{\mu_0}$ | Casson constant, $k_1^2$ is the Casson viscosity |
| `N_CY` | $n$ | $0.9$ | index of the Carreau–Yasuda model |
| `MODEL_CONSTANT_A` | $a$ | $1.5$ | constant of the Carreau–Yasuda model |
| `CHAR_TIME_CONSTANT` | $\lambda$ | $3.313\,\mathrm{s}$ | time constant of the Carreau–Yasuda model |
| `MU_ZERO` | $\mu_\text{zero}$ | $1.45\, \mu_0$ | zero shear viscosity of the Carreau–Yasuda model |
| `MU_INF` | $\mu_\infty$ | $\mu_0 / 10$ | infinite shear viscosity of the Carreau–Yasuda model |
| `N_PL` | | $0.708$ | power-law index of the reference profile for the Carreau–Yasuda model |

: Parameters of `nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d`, as set in `setGetParameters()` in `case.h`. They can be overridden on the command line, e.g. `./nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d --VISCOSITY_MODEL 1`. {#tbl-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-params}

#### Validation

The simulation runs for the full simulated time.
Every $T/10$ and at the end, the example prints the absolute and relative $L^1$, $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ errors of the velocity against the analytical profile, and every $T/100$ it writes the velocity, the pressure, the analytical velocity and the local relaxation frequency to the VTK output.

With the default parameters, the relative $L^2$ error of the velocity at the end is $0.61\,\%$ for the Newtonian and $0.75\,\%$ for the power-law model.
@fig-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-profile compares both profiles with the analytical ones: at the same pressure gradient, the shear-thinning power-law fluid flows more than twice as fast as the Newtonian fluid, and its profile is flatter.

![Velocity profiles of `nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d` along $y$ through the pipe axis at $x = L/2$ at the end of the simulation, for the Newtonian and the power-law model at the same pressure gradient, compared with the analytical profiles.](/examples/laminar/nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d/doc/fig/profile/profile.svg){width="60%" #fig-nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d-profile .lightbox}

The program in the subdirectory `eoc/` uses the same `case.h` and runs the selected model for the resolutions `EOC_RESOLUTIONS` one after the other. At the end, it prints the errors and the experimental orders of convergence between consecutive resolutions.

#### Files

```
nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d/
├── nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d.cpp       main(): selects the viscosity model and runs the simulation
├── case.h                             Case type, parameters, viscosity models, geometry, lattice, error norms and output
├── eoc/
│   ├── nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d.cpp   convergence study over EOC_RESOLUTIONS
│   └── Makefile
└── Makefile
```

The results are written to `tmp/<model>/`, for example `tmp/Newtonian/`, in the directory the example is run from: `vtkData/nonNewtonianPoiseuille3d.pvd` opens all time steps in ParaView. The convergence study writes to `tmp/<model>_eoc/`.
